subject: Aegis DPA: data retention, backup & DR carve-out — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Amara Singh <amara@aegisclinical.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Rao <priyanka.rao@aegisclinical.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: DPA retention + backup carve-out question

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's DPA and flagged the retention & backup sections. Two items that are blocking execution on our side:

1) Aegis needs confirmation that backups and immutable DR snapshots will be excluded from customer-driven deletion requests for a defined short period (we propose 90 days) because our disaster recovery and forensic processes rely on immutable backups.

2) We need clarity on service of data destruction for EU-origin datasets and whether Redwood will rely on subprocessors (and which ones) for backup storage.

I attached our annotated redline (Retention_Tabular_Specs.xlsx) and included a clean copy of your DPA for reference. Can we get a concrete suggested carve-out text from Redwood legal so our counsel can review? Also — will DocuSign execution be acceptable?

Best,
Amara
Head of InfoSec, Aegis Clinical
(attachment: Retention_Tabular_Specs.xlsx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Amara Singh <amara@aegisclinical.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA retention + backup carve-out question

Amara —

Thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet, that helps. High level response from our side:

- We understand the need for immutable backups for DR/forensics. Redwood can accept a limited carve-out that excludes immutable backups from customer-initiated deletion requests for a short retention window.
- We typically recommend 30 days as the operational default (to balance compliance and recovery), but we are open to 90 days for regulated customers if we align on a legal hold process and exception controls.
- Subprocessors: our backups in this deployment use a managed S3-compatible storage provider (we list subprocessors in the DPA appendix). We can add a specific callout naming that provider and confirm EU transfer mechanisms (SCCs + our data transfer policy).

I attached our current redline (DPA_Aegis_redline_v2.docx) with proposed language that tries to be surgical and time-boxed. If that looks okay I can route to our legal team to sign via DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
- Vanessa & Karthik: finalize language with Vivek's input (ops)
- Vanessa: send updated redline back to Aegis legal + DocuSign envelope by Mon

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(attachment: DPA_Aegis_redline_v2.docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:51:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA retention + backup carve-out question

Vanessa — quick notes inline for the proposed carve-out:

- We should explicitly tie the carve-out to 'immutable backups and DR snapshots' to avoid broadening it to primary deletion controls.
- Add a clause: "Redwood will, upon receiving a verified deletion request, mark primary copies for deletion in accordance with the DPA and will retain immutable backup copies for the carve-out period only; backups will be overwritten or purged after the carve-out period unless subject to a legal hold."
- For EU data: confirm that backups stored outside EU will be covered by SCCs and that the named subprocessor has contracts supporting those flows.

Also, Vivek — can you confirm whether we support 90-day immutable retention in our Dedicated and Private deployments without additional work? If extra ops/config required, call it out so we can surface a potential uplift to Aegis.

Karthik

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA retention + backup carve-out question

Karthik / Vanessa —

Operational note: 90 days is supported technically but depends on the storage class and lifecycle policies for the customer's tenant. For Hosted customers we'd need to enable a retention flag and ensure immutability via object lock on the backup bucket; that is a short config change and we can do it but it requires a runbook update and billing note for increased snapshot retention costs. For Dedicated / Private, customers can configure retention themselves; we provide guidance.

I propose the legal text: 
"Notwithstanding Section X (Deletion of Customer Data), immutable backups and DR snapshots containing Customer Data shall be excluded from Customer-initiated deletion requests for a period not to exceed 90 days (the 'Backup Carve-out Period'). During the Backup Carve-out Period Redwood will ensure backups are stored with industry-standard immutability controls and will, upon expiration of the carve-out period or upon receipt of an enforceable legal hold notice, permanently purge such backups in accordance with agreed procedures. The parties agree that this carve-out applies only to immutable backup copies and does not affect deletion requirements for primary production copies of Customer Data."

I'll also add a sentence naming the subprocessor ("AcmeStorage Inc.") in an appendix and confirm that SCCs apply for cross-border backup storage.

Vivek
Senior Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Amara Singh <amara@aegisclinical.com>, Priyanka Rao <priyanka.rao@aegisclinical.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA retention + backup carve-out question — proposed language & DocuSign

Amara / Priyanka —

Attached is the updated DPA redline with the carve-out language Vivek drafted (see page 4 of the redline). Key points:

• Carve-out limited to immutable backups and DR snapshots; capped at 90 days by default.
• We will implement object-lock-backed immutability for backups and confirm the subprocessor (AcmeStorage Inc.) is contractually bound by SCCs for EU-origin data.
• Cost note: 90-day backup retention may incur incremental snapshot storage; I'll include this in the order form if you proceed.

If that aligns with Aegis counsel, we're happy to finalize the redline and send the DocuSign envelope. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/tx/0A1B2C3D4E5F (attached summary: DocuSign_Envelope_Summary.pdf).

Proposed ask: please confirm by EOD Wed so we can get this executed before your go/no-go on Nov 30.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
